methods.description: Lists the caller’s own tasks, most recently changed first (by status timestamp, then task id ascending); a caller holding `bureau.tasks:read` lists every owner’s. `contextId` returns only that context’s tasks in its current incarnation, `origin` only the tasks recorded with an origin of that kind (`chat`, `person`, `schedule`, `api`, `agent`, `goal`, or `parent`), `parentRunId` only the subordinate tasks of that run (the children it started, the attempts of a goal, the steps of a workflow instance), `parentContextId` only the child runs started from any run in that context (a reloaded chat lists the children of every run in its thread this way), `siblingsOf` only the tasks that share a parent run with the named task, that task excluded, `workflow` only the tasks that ran on that workflow type (`workflow.type` on each task says which), `attention` only the tasks whose `attention` lists that kind (`stalled` or `looping`), `failedStep` only the tasks that failed at the step with that label (`failure.step.label`), `retrying` only the tasks with a step on a second or later try (`true`) or with none (`false`), and `statusTimestampAfter` (ISO 8601) only tasks whose status timestamp is strictly later. Pages with `limit` (1 to 100, default 50, free to change between pages) and `pageToken`; `nextPageToken` is `null` when no entries remain. The first page of a listing with a next page records the listing, and every later page returns the tasks exactly as they matched then, so a task that changes mid-enumeration keeps its place and appears once; a task removed since is skipped, so a page can hold fewer than `limit` tasks. A token is opaque, valid for 15 minutes from the first page, and only with the principal, reach, wire projection (never the one of A2A `ListTasks`), and filters (`contextId`, `agentName`, `status`, `origin`, `parentRunId`, `parentContextId`, `siblingsOf`, `workflow`, `attention`, `failedStep`, `retrying`, `engineRuns`, `statusTimestampAfter`) it was issued for, and only while the context is the incarnation it was issued for; any other token is `InvalidParams`. The schedule tick’s runs and the instances of workflow files are listed too, read from the engine, for a caller that may read the deployment’s workflows. A principal holds at most 16 live listings, and starting another ends its oldest.

A run that did not fail, one that is still going included, is `Unprocessable` with `data.reason` `run-not-failed` and a `remediation`; a workflow instance whose run state or timeline the Bureau cannot read, because it has no durable engine, is `UnsupportedCapability` (`durable-engine`), never `run-not-failed`. An agent run is read with the access `bureau.tasks.get` asks and a workflow instance with the access `bureau.workflows.runs.get` asks; any other run, a run the caller may not read, and a run that does not exist are all `NotFound`.

methods.description: Cancels one of the caller’s own tasks; a caller holding `bureau.tasks:write` cancels any owner’s. The receipt says where the cancellation stands: `cancel-requested` (the run has not stopped), `canceled` (a durable run stopped with no cleanup evidence to report), `cleanup-pending`, `cleaned-up`, `cleanup-failed`, `cleanup-unresolved` (cleanup could not be confirmed and may still be running, so nothing is promised about external effects), `unknown-outcome` (an external effect may or may not have happened), or `rejected` (nothing is applied). methods.description: Deletes one of the caller’s own contexts; a caller holding `bureau.contexts:write` deletes any owner’s. The deletion fences the context first, so a new task or session input for it reads as a context that does not exist, then cancels and awaits every live task in it, then removes the context and empties its tasks’ message histories. Once the context is gone and its runs have ended, its content is purged: the event history of the context and of each run, the runs’ workflows and checkpoints, their interactive surfaces, the context’s session input and A2A history, the records of their reviews, and the runs they delegated to go, and their audit entries are redacted (the entries stay, as proof the runs happened). A purge that fails is finished by the next maintenance pass or boot, and a second pass ten minutes after it removes what a late writer added. The deletion also records the context’s id, its owner and when it was deleted, and nothing else, under the thread’s lease before anything is removed, so an AG-UI start or resume on that id is refused as `THREAD_DELETED` rather than creating the chat again. The `receipt` is `applied` (no task was live), or the aggregate of the cancelled tasks’ cleanup, the least settled winning: `cleanup-pending`, `cleanup-unresolved`, `unknown-outcome`, `cleanup-failed`, `cleaned-up`; `tasks` lists each. `rejected` (reason `shutting-down`) means admission is closed and nothing was applied. `waitMilliseconds` (default 0) waits that long for outstanding cleanup acknowledgements. With `dryRun: true` nothing is deleted, fenced, cancelled or recorded: the answer is `{ dryRun: true, target, effects }`, whose `runs-in-progress` effect counts the live tasks the delete would cancel (none once Bureau is shutting down, when the real call is `rejected`), and a context that is missing, not the caller’s or on a Bureau that keeps no sessions answers the fault the real call answers.

methods.description: Changes one setting of one of the caller’s own contexts; the request carries exactly one of `override`, `effort` and `permissionMode`, and one with none or more than one is `InvalidParams` naming the field. `override` (`{ provider, model }`) switches the context to a model, which must be one `bureau.agents.models` lists for the context’s agent; for an agent with `limits.cost`, a model the catalog has no US-dollar price for is `InvalidParams` naming `override`, because its spend could not be counted against the budget. `effort` (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`) sets the reasoning effort, which must be one the deployment’s model catalog holds, and `bureau.contexts.get` reads the settled one back. `permissionMode` (`always`, `on-changes`, `allow-all` or `read-only`) sets how readily the chat’s tool calls ask a person: `read-only` denies every tool that is not read-only, `always` asks on every call, `allow-all` skips the asks `on-changes` would raise (never a tool set to `always` or `blocked`), and the default `on-changes` asks as each tool’s own setting says; `bureau.contexts.get` reads it back. The mode governs every tool of the chat’s runs, for any kind of agent, Bureau’s own included: `decide` is a read, and `scheduleWakeup` a change that `always` denies as well, since no approval could run it. Only `requestHumanInput`, which just asks a person, stands outside it. A child Bureau started, however deep and even one detached from a parent that has ended, takes the mode at its next tool call; it cannot be put to a person, so in `always` it runs no tool, and a call `on-changes` would ask about is refused. A child Bureau cannot configure is outside the mode and is not held to it; that includes one an agent’s own `createSubagentTool` runs and a task a remote agent runs for a `createPeerCallTool` call. A child whose agent exposes no run options is refused, not started, when a Bureau-owned run dispatches it, an approved call that resumed included. The mode a child takes is the stricter of its chat’s and its own `on-changes`, so `allow-all` does not loosen it; a chat deleted since the child started holds the child to `read-only`. A mode is read at each tool call, so it is in force from the next tool call; the model and effort are used from the live run’s next step. Each is kept for the context’s later runs, across a restart; a context with no run in progress takes it for its next run. `commandId` is the caller’s own identifier for the command, `expectedRevision` the `configVersion` (`bureau.contexts.get`) the caller read. The answer is Bureau’s admission outcome as data: `accepted` with the command and its `configVersion`; `replayed` for an exact retry of a `commandId`; `conflict` for a `commandId` used for another request; `rejected` with a `failure.reason`: `model-not-allowed` for a model the context’s agent does not allow (decided now, with nothing changed, and the same answer to every retry), `stale-revision` for an `expectedRevision` behind the context’s `configVersion`, `shutting-down` when Bureau is closing and nothing was decided (a retry after a restart is admitted normally), or `policy-denied` for a model or effort the deployment’s catalog does not hold; and `unsupported-capability` with its `reason`. An archived context (`bureau.contexts.archive`) takes no command: it is a `Conflict` fault with reason `context-archived`, and nothing is decided or logged. Another owner’s context, a missing one, and an operator that does not own the context answer `NotFound`, since Bureau admits steering only under the session’s own authority. Requires `bureau.contexts:write` to act for any other owner; no scope is needed for the caller’s own. The call writes no audit entry.

permissionMode.description: The permission mode to set: `always` asks on every call, `on-changes` (the default) asks as each tool’s own setting says, `allow-all` skips the asks `on-changes` would raise, and `read-only` denies every tool that is not read-only. It governs every tool of the chat’s runs, for any kind of agent, Bureau’s own included: `decide` is a read, and `scheduleWakeup` a change that `always` denies as well, since no approval could run it. Only `requestHumanInput`, which just asks a person, stands outside it. A child Bureau started, however deep and even one detached from a parent that has ended, takes the mode at its next tool call; it cannot be put to a person, so in `always` it runs no tool, and a call `on-changes` would ask about is refused. A child Bureau cannot configure is outside the mode and is not held to it; that includes one an agent’s own `createSubagentTool` runs and a task a remote agent runs for a `createPeerCallTool` call. A child whose agent exposes no run options is refused, not started, when a Bureau-owned run dispatches it, an approved call that resumed included. The mode a child takes is the stricter of its chat’s and its own `on-changes`, so `allow-all` does not loosen it; a chat deleted since the child started holds the child to `read-only`. Exactly one of `override`, `effort` and `permissionMode` is sent.

methods.description: Branches one of the caller’s own contexts at the end of a turn: a new context that shares the history through `throughMessageId`, which must be the last assistant reply of a run that has ended (`completed`, errored or aborted), is owned by the caller, and records its lineage (`parentContextId`, `forkedFromMessageId`). `throughMessageId: null` branches before the first message: the new context starts empty, records `parentContextId` and a `null` `forkedFromMessageId`. Editing a sent message is this call at the reply before it, then a new run of the edited text on the new context (`bureau.contexts.input` reaches only a live run, so an idle fork answers it `session-terminal`); the original is left unchanged. An earlier turn can be branched while a later run of the context is still live; the live run’s own replies cannot. The parent’s latest model override is carried onto the new context as `<commandId>:model`, and its admission outcome is returned as `carriedOverride`, `null` when the parent had none; a refused admission (the model is no longer allowed) leaves the new context in place on the agent’s default. The parent’s effort is carried the same way as `<commandId>:effort` and returned as `carriedEffort`, and its permission mode as `<commandId>:permission-mode` and `carriedPermissionMode`, so a branch of a read-only chat is read-only. `commandId` is the caller’s own identifier: an exact retry, even after a restart, returns the original answer and creates nothing more. The command’s identity is the caller’s owner, the context and the `commandId`, so an operator and the owner retrying one `commandId` make two forks, and a settled command is kept for 24 hours, after which an exact retry branches again. A message the context does not hold is `NotFound`. A message that is not the last assistant reply of an ended run is a `Conflict` with reason `not-a-branch-point`; a run with a tool approval waiting `branch-with-pending-approval`; a reply with a tool call that has no result `branch-with-unresolved-tool-call`; and a `commandId` already used for another message `command-conflict`. A Bureau that is shutting down is `Unavailable` with reason `shutting-down`. Another owner’s context and a missing one answer `NotFound`. Branching another owner’s context copies its history, so it requires both `bureau.contexts:read` and `bureau.contexts:write`; a caller holding only one of them is answered `NotFound`, as for a context it may not see. No scope is needed for the caller’s own. The call writes no audit entry.

methods.description: Replaces the latest answer of one of the caller’s own contexts with a new one from the model, without running any tool. `messageId` must be the last row of the context and the last assistant reply of its newest run, which has ended, with no tool approval pending and no tool call left without a result. The model is asked once, over the history before that answer, with a toolbox that holds no tool, on the model the context’s steering names now (or the agent’s default) as the model policy judges it now; the new answer keeps the message id, and every other row (the user’s message, earlier replies, tool calls, tool results and approvals) is kept as it was. The model is asked under the hooks a run’s step runs: the Bureau’s identity prompt and guardrails, and the agent’s own. An answer that asks for a tool is `Unprocessable` with reason `answer-has-tool-calls`, and a model that fails, that policy refuses, or whose answer a guardrail halts is `Unavailable` with reason `generation-failed`; neither changes the history. The replacement is one compare-and-swap on the context, fenced on the revision the call read: a new turn, a steering change, a deletion, or a new context under the id since then is a `Conflict` with reason `history-changed`, and nothing is written. An aborted request is `Unavailable` with reason `aborted` unless the new answer was already committed. `commandId` is the caller’s own identifier: only the call that claims it asks the model, and an exact retry, even after a restart, returns the original answer without asking it again. A retry while the first call is still going is answered from that call’s committed receipt, or as a `Conflict` with reason `command-in-doubt`; the same `commandId` for another message is a `Conflict` with reason `command-conflict`. A message the context does not hold is `NotFound`; any other message that cannot be regenerated is a `Conflict` with reason `not-a-branch-point`, `branch-with-pending-approval`, `branch-with-unresolved-tool-call`, or `not-latest-answer`. An archived context (`bureau.contexts.archive`) asks no model: it is a `Conflict` with reason `context-archived`. A Bureau that is shutting down is `Unavailable` with reason `shutting-down`. Another owner’s context and a missing one answer `NotFound`. Regenerating another owner’s context reads and rewrites its history, so it requires both `bureau.contexts:read` and `bureau.contexts:write`; a caller holding only one of them is answered `NotFound`. No scope is needed for the caller’s own. The call writes no audit entry.

methods.description: Removes the last unfinished turn of one of the caller’s own contexts: the rows `runId` wrote after the person’s message that started it (its replies, tool calls, tool results and the answers given to its questions). The person’s message is kept. `runId` must be the context’s last run, and it must have ended without finishing: the person stopped it, or it failed. A run still going, or waiting on an approval or a question, is a `Conflict` with reason `turn-running` (cancel it first); one that finished normally is `turn-finished`; one whose process stopped before it recorded its end is `turn-outcome-unknown`; a later run or a row the run did not write after its turn is `not-latest-turn`; a follow-up the person sent that was delivered into the turn is `follow-up-delivered`, and one still queued is `follow-ups-queued`; a run that wrote nothing is `nothing-to-discard`. A run the context does not have is `NotFound`. The removal is one compare-and-swap on the context, fenced on the revision the call read: a change since then is a `Conflict` with reason `history-changed`, and nothing is written. The same commit records an audit entry, `context.turn-discarded`, with the run, the command and how many rows went. `commandId` is the caller’s own identifier: an exact retry, even after a restart, returns the original result and removes nothing more; a retry while the first call is still going is answered from that call’s committed receipt, or as a `Conflict` with reason `command-in-doubt`; the same `commandId` for another run is a `Conflict` with reason `command-conflict`. The run’s task is kept as it is: it still says how the run ended. An archived context is a `Conflict` with reason `context-archived`. A Bureau that is shutting down is `Unavailable` with reason `shutting-down`. Another owner’s context and a missing one answer `NotFound`. Discarding another owner’s turn reads and rewrites its history, so it requires both `bureau.contexts:read` and `bureau.contexts:write`; a caller holding only one of them is answered `NotFound`. No scope is needed for the caller’s own.

methods.description: Lets the last stopped turn of one of the caller’s own contexts go on. A continuation run starts on the stored conversation, the partial reply included, with no message from the person, and writes a new assistant turn after the partial reply; the answer names it as `runId`, and the stopped run as `resumedRunId`. `runId` must be the context’s last run, stopped by the person or failed on a cause worth trying again (finish reason `error`). The start is one atomic write to the context that adds a hidden continuation row naming the stopped run and the command and judges the history again, so a message, a discard or another resume that lands first wins and this one is refused. `commandId` is the caller’s own identifier: a retry answers the run the first call started, after a restart too, and never starts a second; the same `commandId` for another run is a `Conflict` with reason `command-conflict`. Each refusal is a `Conflict` and starts nothing: `not-latest-turn` (a later run, or the turn already went on), `turn-running`, `turn-awaiting-person` (it goes on once the approval or question is answered), `turn-recovering` (the run’s process stopped, and the Bureau that next boots goes on with it from its checkpoint or ends it when it cannot), `turn-finished` (a reply cut at the token limit included), `run-not-resumable` (a failure going on would meet again), `turn-interrupted-call` (the turn stopped inside a tool call, which going on would run again unasked), `follow-up-delivered`, `follow-ups-queued` and `nothing-to-resume`. A run the context does not have is `NotFound`. An archived context is a `Conflict` with reason `context-archived`. A Bureau that is shutting down is `Unavailable` with reason `shutting-down`. It is owner only: the continuation runs as the owner’s chat, so no operator scope lets anyone else resume it, and another owner’s context and a missing one answer `NotFound`, whatever run they name. No scope is needed for the caller’s own.

methods.description: Archives one of the caller’s own contexts; a caller holding `bureau.contexts:write` archives any owner’s. An archived context accepts no new work: starting a task in it, `bureau.contexts.input`, `bureau.contexts.steer`, `bureau.contexts.regenerate`, `bureau.contexts.discardturn` and `bureau.contexts.resumeturn` are each a `Conflict` with reason `context-archived` until it is unarchived (`bureau.contexts.unarchive`), and a schedule’s fire into it fails; reading, renaming, deleting, forking, forgetting grants and the window keep working. `bureau.contexts.list` and `get` show when in `archivedAt`, and `list` filters by it with `archived`. A context with a task running, or waiting on an approval or an answer, is a `Conflict` with reason `context-busy`, and nothing is stored: stop or answer the task first. A goal’s session (origin `goal`) cannot be archived, because the goal writes its attempts to it whatever it records: it is a `Conflict` with reason `context-not-archivable`, and the goal is stopped with `bureau.goals.cancel` instead. Archiving is not activity: the context’s `updatedAt`, and so its place in a listing, does not move. Archiving an archived context is not an error: it answers `changed: false` with the time it was first archived, so a retry is safe. Another owner’s context and a missing one answer `NotFound`. A Bureau that is shutting down is `Unavailable` with reason `shutting-down`. Answers a receipt, `{ id, changed, archivedAt }`, and nothing else of the context. The call writes no audit entry.

methods.description: Returns how full one of the caller’s own contexts’ windows is; a caller holding `bureau.contexts:read` reads any owner’s. `usedEstimated` is an estimate (four characters to a token; an attachment by its byte size) of the prompt the context’s next step would send, and always equals the sum of `categories`, which lists `system` (the instructions), `tools` (the schemas offered), `messages` (the conversation after any compaction), `memory` (recalled memory) and `attachments` (media) once each, in that order. `usedReported` is the provider’s own count, never an estimate: the input tokens (fresh, cache-read and cache-written) of the context’s latest step, or `null` when there is none or the provider reported none; it describes the request that step sent, so it lags the estimate by that step’s reply and tool results. `maxTokens` is the context window of the model that would answer, from the model catalog: the context’s steered model (`bureau.contexts.steer`), else its agent’s default, and `null` when neither names a catalog row. It works for an idle context, a context with no run (estimated from its agent’s definition), and a running one, which it reads without waiting on the run. A chat saves its rows when its run ends (a scheduled fire saves after every step), so a chat mid-run still holds the rows it started with (its instructions and the input): `usedEstimated` can then lag `usedReported`, which counts the steps already sent (once the run ends, the reverse holds: `usedReported` predates the reply). The latest step is looked for among the context’s 50 newest tasks, and `usedReported` is `null` when none of them recorded a step. A managed-asset attachment is sized from its stored byte length. It calls no model and writes nothing. Another owner’s context answers as a missing one does. The response carries counts only, no message text.

methods.description: Writes the definition of version `revision` back to the agent’s file as a new revision, if the file still hashes to `expectedHash`, and returns the new `hash` and `revision`. The definition’s `references` list is restored, but the documents are not: they are whatever those paths name when the file is read again (the version’s `referenceDigests` say what they were), and `examples` are not restored either; the file keeps what it has. A file that moved since is a `StaleRevision` fault whose `currentRevision` is the hash now on disk; a definition that no longer resolves (its model or a tool is gone from the deployment, a reference document is missing or too large (`missing-reference`, `reference-too-large`), a guardrail or interceptor it lists is no longer contributed (`reference-unresolved`), a guardrail’s schema no longer accepts the configuration it gives (`invalid-guardrail-configuration`), it enables compaction with no summarizer, the `modelPolicy` deployment or Bureau layer now forbids its model (`model-policy-denied`), or its model does not support its `effort` (`effort-not-supported`)) is `Unprocessable`; an unknown version is `NotFound`; each writes nothing. methods.description: Starts the failed `listener` of the workflow `id`’s contributed trigger at once, with its backoff cleared, and answers `{ id, listener }` once the attempt has settled: a listener that fails again is `failed` with its next `retryAt`. methods.description: Resolves a pending review of one of the caller’s own runs as the authenticated caller; the reviewer is never a payload field. A caller holding `bureau.reviews:resolve` resolves any owner’s. `reject` requires a `reason`. The `receipt` is `applied` (including a landed reject, which `decision` reports) or `superseded`. Resolving a review that is already resolved answers `Conflict` when the call asks for a different decision than the one recorded (a resolver that lost), and 404 when it repeats that decision, until command receipts exist; one the caller may not resolve answers 404. `remember: true` on approving a tool approval also allows its tool for the rest of the chat: the next ask for it in that chat that the agent file would make by `on-changes` runs without asking, and no other chat, fork, tool, `always` or `blocked` value, agent-wide always mode or read-only restriction is affected; the response says `remembered`. Resolving a tool approval also writes its outcome into the session’s conversation: the executed result on approve, an error result carrying the reason on deny and reject, each replacing the pending `action_required` result in place, so a run started next on the session answers an up-to-date conversation. The outcome row’s metadata records who decided and when, with the note, the sentence the tool asked with, and the `decisionSurface` the call gave, under `approvalDecision`. A `superseded` receipt writes nothing. A tool approval does not park its run, so once this call decides the last pending review of a chat’s run (approve, deny or reject), it starts the run that answers the decisions, as the chat’s own resume does: one run, owned by the chat’s owner whoever decided, under a command id of the decided run alone, so the chat’s resume of the same reviews, a decision racing it, and a retry all continue with that one run. `continuation` says which run (`started`), or why none could start (`not-started`, the decision having taken effect); it is absent while another review of the run is pending, for a run that is not a chat’s, and for a human wait, whose answer continues its parked run. Approving a human wait takes an `answer`; when the review has an `inputSchema` the answer is checked against it before anything is decided, and one that does not fit answers `InvalidParams` with `data.issues` (`path` rooted at `answer`, `message`, and `code`, the schema keyword that failed) and leaves the review pending. `round` is the round of the review the caller read (`bureau.reviews.get` and `list` return it): a re-gated approval keeps its id and advances its round, so a decision made on round N is refused with a `Conflict` once the review is at another round, before anything is decided, written, or audited. A `Conflict` whose `reason` begins `REVIEW_ROUND_CHANGED: ` is that refusal (nothing took effect; read the review again); one that begins `APPROVAL_OUTCOME_NOT_WRITTEN: ` means the decision took effect (the tool ran or was refused) and only that write failed; one that begins `REVIEW_ALREADY_RESOLVED: ` (COR-2426) means the review was already resolved with another decision, so nothing took effect and it is no longer waiting; any other `Conflict` is a resolver that lost. Omit `round` and the call is not fenced.

methods.description: Cancels one of the caller’s own goals; a caller holding `bureau.goals:write` cancels any owner’s, and anyone else is answered `NotFound`. The goal’s controller and its attempt’s run are stopped, and the receipt’s `outcome` says how far that has got: it is an answer about durable state read back, never about a request merely sent. `expectedRevision`, when given, is compared inside the store’s compare-and-swap that records the cancellation: a goal that has changed since is a `StaleRevision` fault whose `currentRevision` is the revision now current, and nothing is written. The write scope does not imply the read scope, so the receipt carries the status and revision and nothing else of the goal. A repeated cancel has the same effect. With `dryRun: true` nothing is cancelled and no event or audit entry is written: the answer is `{ dryRun: true, target, effects }`, whose `runs-in-progress` effect counts the attempt runs the cancel would stop, and a goal that is missing, not the caller’s, or at another `revision` than `expectedRevision` answers the fault the real call answers.

methods.description: Changes one of the caller’s own goals for the attempts it has not yet made (COR-2017); a caller holding `bureau.goals:write` changes any owner’s, and anyone else is answered `NotFound`. It names at least one of `prompt`, `agentName`, `validator`, and `maximumAttempts`, and `expectedRevision`, which is compared inside the store’s compare-and-swap that writes the change: a goal that has changed since is a `StaleRevision` fault whose `currentRevision` is the revision now current, and nothing is written. An attempt already made keeps the validator it was checked against, an attempt in flight keeps the prompt it started with, and no attempt is started. Under the default `continue` conversation the first retry opened after a prompt change is turned with the new prompt and then the validator’s feedback, and every later retry is the feedback alone, because the transcript then holds the prompt. `agentName` is the agent the attempts opened from now on run as: an attempt already opened keeps the agent it was opened under, which its record carries, and the ownership, fence and session checks read that agent. It changes only while an attempt is in flight, because a controller starting an attempt reads the agent and claims its run before the record says the attempt exists. A goal that has ended, or whose cancellation is recorded, is a `Conflict`; so is another agent while no attempt is in flight (`agent-between-attempts`), a limit that leaves no room for another attempt, and a new limit while the goal’s last allowed attempt is in flight (`data.reason` says which). An agent the caller may not name, or the catalog lacks, is `NotFound`; an agent that cannot run durably, a validator the Bureau lacks, or one that cannot supply the determinism the goal requires, is `Unprocessable`. The write scope does not imply the read scope, so the receipt carries the status and revision and nothing else of the goal.

methods.description: Lists what the agent `agentId` remembers of the caller’s chats with it, newest first. Requires `bureau.memory:read`, which grants no one else’s memory: a caller without it is `Forbidden`. A memory that was corrected is not listed, its correction is; a quarantined or revoked one is not either. With `state` `quarantined` it lists instead the caller’s quarantined memories, newest first, each with `quarantine`: `at` (when it was quarantined), `by` (`admission` when the admission checks held it as it was written, `owner` when the caller or an earlier quarantine of what it derives from did, `recall` when a recall guardrail withheld it), and `detector` and `category`, the guardrail that held it and the category it reported, both `null` when `by` is `owner`; `quarantine` is absent when the ledger does not explain the memory. They are the memories `bureau.memory.quarantine.release` can release. Inspecting flagged content is a governance act, so `state` `quarantined` requires `bureau.memory:govern` instead of `bureau.memory:read`: a caller without it is `Forbidden` whether or not it has quarantined memories, and a caller that holds only `bureau.memory:read` still lists what is in use as before. Pages with `limit` (1 to 100, default 50) and `offset`; `nextOffset` is `null` on the last page. A Bureau with no governed memory answers `UnsupportedCapability`.

methods.description: Reads one memory of the agent `agentId` with its lineage and history: `memory` (its text, class and `kind`, source and `writer`, trust, creation time and the chat, `sessionId`, that produced it); `lineage`, read from the governance ledger: `runId`, the run that wrote it (`null` for one an operator wrote), `corrects`, the memory this one replaced, and `correctedBy`, the memory that replaced it; and `history`, each earlier version a correction replaced, the most recent first, with its text, kind, writer, trust, when it was written and when it was corrected (empty for a memory never corrected). A person’s correction is written by the person, so it reads `writer` `person` and `trust` `verified` while its history keeps what the agent first wrote. A corrected memory is no longer listed or searched, but is read here, which is how a correction is followed back. Another owner’s memory, a missing one, and a quarantined or revoked one are answered `NotFound`, except a memory its owner shared with the caller (`bureau.memory.share`): the grantee names the owner in `ownerId` and reads it, with an empty `lineage`, since the ledger’s history is the owner’s alone, until the owner revokes the share. methods.description: Adds one memory to what the agent `agentId` remembers of the caller, in the caller’s own words, and answers `outcome` `added` with the memory as the list shows it. It is written by the caller as an `operator` source, so it is `verified` and governed memory’s ledger records a `memory.write.admitted` event under the caller’s owner; `bureau.memory.get` answers its `lineage` with a `null` `runId`. It is stored as the `kind` given, a `fact` (governed memory’s `semantic` class) by default or a `how-to` (its `procedural` class), either kept until a correction supersedes it and never swept as chat memory is, and belongs to no chat, so its `sessionId` is `null` and deleting a chat leaves it. A memory that memory does not admit (its content policy, its quota) is `Unprocessable` with `data.reason` `memory-not-admitted`, and nothing is stored. Content the admission detectors flag is stored quarantined for an inspector, and never listed, searched, read, exported or recalled, so the answer is `outcome` `held` with the stored record’s `id` and no `memory`; this is data and not a fault because only `reason` travels with a fault, and the `id` is the caller’s only name for the record. `bureau.memory.forget` with that `id` removes it (a quarantined memory is otherwise kept indefinitely, and only `bureau.memory.quarantine.release`, once it passes the admission checks again, returns it to use), and a caller that does not remove it leaves it stored. A blank `content`, or one longer than 32768 characters, is `InvalidParams`. An agent that is not in the catalog, or one the caller may not name, is `NotFound`. The call is not idempotent: repeating it adds the memory again. A caller that can own no memory is `Forbidden` with `data.reason` `no owner of record`. Requires `bureau.memory:write`; a caller without it is `Forbidden`.

methods.description: Deletes one memory of the agent `agentId` as a source deletion, and answers the deletion `receipt` as data with `deletion`, the status of the receipt row that removes the record. Once `deletion` is `completed` the record never appears in a list, a search, a read or a recall. `exempt` means a legal hold keeps it stored and listed, and the deletion resumes when the hold is released; `failed` means the step that removes it failed, and forgetting it again retries; `pending` means it is not settled. The receipt’s other targets settle as Bureau’s maintenance pass runs: the copy of recalled text persisted in a conversation is not scrubbed, so that target stays pending until its deadline and then fails. Another owner’s memory and a missing one are answered `NotFound`; a memory derived from others is `Unprocessable`. Requires `bureau.memory:write`; a caller without it is `Forbidden`. With `dryRun: true` nothing is deleted and no memory event is recorded, not even the denial of a refused call: the answer is `{ dryRun: true, target, effects }`, whose `memories` effect counts the record the deletion starts with, as a floor (`atLeast`): the summaries derived from it are removed with it and are not counted, and a legal hold on it keeps it stored; a memory that is missing, another owner’s or derived from others answers the fault the real call answers.

methods.description: Corrects one memory of the agent `agentId` by superseding it with `content`. The successor is written by the caller as an `operator` source, in the original’s memory class and the same collection; the original is kept for history, linked from the successor (`corrects`), and no longer listed, searched or recalled, so recall returns only the corrected content. methods.description: Returns one quarantined memory of the agent `agentId` to active use after inspection, when the admission checks that apply now pass it: governed memory scans its text again, as the record’s own source and kind of memory, with the guardrails of the policy in force at the time of the call. The memory alone becomes active, is searchable and listed again, and a `memory.released` ledger event is recorded under the caller’s owner; memories derived from it stay quarantined. A memory the checks hold stays quarantined and is `Unprocessable` with `data.reason` `memory-verification-failed`, and the ledger’s `memory.release.rejected` event names the guardrail that held it for an inspector. Other refusals are `Unprocessable` too, with `data.reason` `memory-derived-record` (a memory derived from another record is never released, and releasing the one it came from leaves it quarantined), `memory-deletion-pending` (a deletion has claimed it), `memory-superseded` (a correction replaced it) and `memory-tampered` (its text no longer matches what was admitted); each records `memory.release.rejected`. Releasing a memory that is already active is not an error: `changed` is `false`. A memory that was revoked, another owner’s memory and a missing one are `NotFound`. Releasing again after a memory is quarantined again, whether by `bureau.memory.quarantine` or because recall withheld it, runs the checks again. Requires `bureau.memory:govern`, which no other memory scope implies; a caller without it is `Forbidden`.

methods.description: Returns audit records, oldest first (or newest first with `order: 'newest'`), as metadata only: `timestamp`, `type`, `resource` (what the record is about), `principal` (the actor), and a few scalar fields in `detail`. No record carries a secret, transcript, tool argument, tool result, or memory content. A caller sees the records about the resources it owns; a caller holding `bureau.audit:read` sees every record, and a record about a resource with no owner is read only through that scope. `runId` narrows to one resource, `type` to one kind, `types` to any of several kinds, `principal` to one actor, and `since` and `until` to a time range (both ends inclusive). `format: 'jsonl'` returns the page as JSON Lines in `body` (one record per line, with the same redaction) instead of `records`, for export. `includeTotal: true` also returns `total`, how many records match and the caller may see. Pages with `limit` (1 to 100, default 50) and `cursor`; `nextCursor` is `null` on the last page, and a page is filled from the records the caller may see, so a cursor advances across any number of records it may not.

methods.description: Appends one base64 chunk to the caller’s own open upload and answers the session with its `receivedBytes`. A chunk that is not base64 is `InvalidParams`; a chunk larger than the handler’s `maxRequestBodyBytes` is refused with 413 before the operation runs. An append that loses to another append to the same session, in this process or any other sharing the store, is `Conflict` with `data.reason: "concurrent-write"`: nothing of it is stored, and the session holds only the chunk that won. A session that already holds a chunk at the next index (left by a writer that stored the chunk and died before it recorded it) answers every append `Conflict` until it expires (`bureau.assets.uploads.abort` discards it). A session holds at most 9999 chunks: the append that would exceed that is refused as `Unprocessable` with `reason: "per-part-limit-exceeded"` and stores nothing, so a client sends chunks large enough to fit its declared length in 9999. methods.description: Creates a hook owned by the caller: when a published Bureau event of one of `events` happens, its `action` runs. `events` may list a kind a running plugin declares, which the hook stores pinned to the kind’s version (`plugin:name@version`, the `version` `bureau.events.catalog` gives) and which fires only while that version is loaded. `action` is `{ type: "webhook", url }` (or `url` alone, its shorthand), `{ type: "start-workflow", workflowId, input? }`, `{ type: "notify", title? }` or `{ type: "plugin", plugin, kind, configuration? }` (an action kind a plugin contributes; its configuration is checked against the kind’s schema, and an unknown kind is `InvalidParams` on `action.kind`). A webhook sends `url` a POST whose body is `{ id, hookId, kind, bureauId, emittedAtMs, test, payload, source? }`, `source` being the plugin whose contribution emitted the event and absent for an event from Bureau core, and whose `X-Signature` header (`t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<body>` under `signingSecret`) lets the receiver verify it; a delivery that fails is retried with backoff and resumed after a restart, and its request, response excerpt and attempts are kept (`bureau.hooks.deliveries`). `signingSecret` is refused for the other actions and is write-only; a webhook created without one gets a secret the Bureau generates (`whsec_` and 24 hexadecimal digits), returned as `signingSecret` on this answer and never again (`null` otherwise). `start-workflow` starts the workflow as the owner, with the event’s payload (or, with `input: "event"`, `{ kind, bureauId, emittedAtMs, payload, source? }`) as its input; input the workflow refuses fails that delivery without a retry, a delivery retried or resumed starts one run, and the events of a run a hook started start nothing (that delivery fails, `Skipped`), so hooks do not chain. A delivery is made for each publication of an event, and the `goal.*` events are at-least-once. It needs a caller allowed to start workflows, and an owner who may (in v1 the deployment’s owner of record), else `Forbidden` (`data.reason: "workflow authority"`); an unknown or paused workflow is `InvalidParams`. `notify` writes the owner a notification per event, once per delivery, and cannot list `notification.created` or a `hook.delivery.*` kind (`InvalidParams` on `events`). The caller needs no scope to own a hook, but needs `bureau.events:observe-all`, because a hook observes the whole Bureau’s events. `scope` makes the hook fire only for one agent, workflow or schedule, read from each event and the Bureau’s records; an event it cannot place is out of scope. A scope some listed kind cannot be told by (`scopes` in `bureau.events.catalog`) is `InvalidParams` on `scope`. An unacceptable URL, event list or secret is `InvalidParams`. A deployment that keeps secrets elsewhere refuses with `Forbidden` (`data.reason: "deployment"`). A Bureau without hooks, or without an encryption key, answers `UnsupportedCapability`.

methods.description: Sends one of a hook’s deliveries again from its record (COR-2022): the request recorded when the delivery was made, with the same body, `X-Delivery-Id` and `Idempotency-Key`, never one rebuilt from the hook as it is now; it is signed with the hook’s current secret. A delivery that was not delivered (`exhausted`, `failed`, `aborted` or `failed-secret`) gets one more attempt, made now, and the answer is its record once that attempt has ended. A `pending` delivery waiting out its backoff is tried now, and the answer is its record at once; one whose attempt is in flight is left to it. A `delivered` delivery is `InvalidParams` on `deliveryId`, and a delivery that is not the hook’s is `NotFound`. A caller retries its own hooks’ deliveries; `bureau.hooks:write` retries any owner’s.

methods.description: Makes a hook of the caller’s own from one the caller may read (COR-2181): the same action, events and scope, off, with no `declaredBy`, so a default hook a plugin declared becomes a hook the owner can change. `name` labels the copy, else it keeps the hook’s own label. The copy is owned by the caller, whoever owned the original, and is checked as `bureau.hooks.create` checks a hook, so it needs `bureau.events:observe-all` (a hook observes the whole Bureau’s events), and a copy of a `start-workflow` hook needs a caller allowed to start workflows. A webhook’s copy gets a signing secret the Bureau generates, shown once as `signingSecret` on the answer (`null` otherwise) and never copied from the original. A caller copies its own hooks, and `bureau.hooks:read` reads any owner’s to copy; another owner’s hook the caller may not read answers `NotFound`, as `bureau.hooks.get` does, and in a workspace a hook of another owner is copied only when it is a webhook for events shared to the workspace. A hook whose plugin no longer offers its action is `InvalidParams` on `action.kind`, because a copy would be checked against a schema that is gone. The copy is made of the hook as it was when the caller was allowed to copy it: a hook that changed in between is a `StaleRevision` fault whose `currentRevision` is the revision now current, and nothing is made.
